desc:
Simulate a cache that holds at most capacity key-value pairs and evicts the least recently used pair when it is full. A pair is "used" whenever it is read by a hit or written. Each operation is a triple [type, key, value]:

  • [0, key, 0] (get): if key is in the cache, report its value and mark it as most recently used; otherwise report -1.
  • [1, key, value] (put): if key is already in the cache, replace its value and mark it as most recently used. Otherwise insert it as the most recently used pair; if the cache already held capacity pairs, first evict the least recently used one.

Return the reported values of all get operations in order. For example with capacity = 2 and ops = [[1,1,10],[1,2,20],[0,1,0],[1,3,30],[0,2,0],[0,3,0],[1,1,11],[0,1,0]] the answer is [10,-1,30,11]: putting key 3 evicts key 2, because key 1 was just read.

Aim for O(1) per operation. This is the classic hash map + doubly linked list design.
constraints: For a get the value field is 0
hints: You need two things at once: find a key quickly, and know which key is the least recently used. One structure per job.

A hash map from key to node finds entries in O(1). A doubly linked list ordered by recency (most recent at the front) can move any node to the front and remove the tail in O(1), because deleting a node needs prev and next.

Use dummy head and tail nodes. Helpers: unlink(node) and push_front(node). A hit is unlink + push_front. A put of a new key on a full cache first removes tail.prev from both the list and the map. Store the key inside each node so you can delete it from the map when you evict it.
editorial: Keep a hash map key -> node and a doubly linked list of nodes ordered from most to least recently used, with sentinel nodes at both ends so that no case is special. Every get hit and every put moves its node to the front; the eviction victim is always the node before the tail sentinel.

Each operation is a map lookup plus a constant number of pointer changes, so it runs in O(1) and the whole script in O(q). The node must remember its key: when you evict the last node you have to delete that key from the map. A singly linked list would not work because removing an arbitrary node in O(1) needs its predecessor.
